nodes.summary: The set of all cluster variables in all seeds obtained from `s` by iterated mutation (Fomin, Williams and Zelevinsky, *Introduction to cluster algebras, Chapters 1–3*, arXiv:1608.05735v5, Definition 3.1.9, the set `𝒳`).
nodes.title: Cluster variables of a seed pattern

nodes.summary: The cluster `(X_i)_{i ∈ n}` of free generators of `ℚ(X_i : i ∈ n) = FractionRing (MvPolynomial n ℤ)`, the ambient field of a labeled seed (Fomin, Williams and Zelevinsky, *Introduction to cluster algebras, Chapters 1–3*, arXiv:1608.05735v5, Definition 3.1.1, with no frozen variables).
nodes.title: Initial cluster of the ambient field

nodes.summary: If positive integers `dᵢ` satisfy `dᵢ bᵢⱼ = -dⱼ bⱼᵢ`, then they also skew-symmetrize `μₖ B` (Fomin, Williams and Zelevinsky, *Introduction to cluster algebras, Chapters 1–3*, arXiv:1608.05735v5, Exercise 2.7.7(1), square case).
nodes.title: Matrix mutation preserves skew-symmetrizability

nodes.summary: An integer square matrix `B` is skew-symmetrizable if there are positive integers `dᵢ` with `dᵢ bᵢⱼ = -dⱼ bⱼᵢ` for all `i, j` (Fomin, Williams and Zelevinsky, *Introduction to cluster algebras, Chapters 1–3*, arXiv:1608.05735v5, Definition 2.7.4).
nodes.title: Skew-symmetrizable integer matrix

nodes.summary: Let `B` be a skew-symmetrizable integer `n × n` matrix and start from the seed `((X_i), B)` in `ℚ(X_i : i ∈ n)`. Every cluster variable of every seed obtained by iterated mutation is a Laurent polynomial in the `X_i` with integer coefficients (Fomin, Williams and Zelevinsky, *Introduction to cluster algebras, Chapters 1–3*, arXiv:1608.05735v5, Theorem 3.3.1, in the case without frozen variables; Fomin and…
nodes.title: Laurent phenomenon (coefficient-free)

nodes.summary: The ring `ℤ[X_i^{±1}]` of Laurent polynomials with integer coefficients in the initial cluster, as the `ℤ`-subalgebra of `FractionRing (MvPolynomial n ℤ)` generated by the `X_i` and their inverses (Fomin, Williams and Zelevinsky, *Introduction to cluster algebras, Chapters 1–3*, arXiv:1608.05735v5, Theorem 3.3.1, where the conclusion is membership in this ring).
nodes.title: Laurent polynomials in the initial cluster

nodes.summary: Mutating twice in the same direction `k` returns the original matrix, `μₖ (μₖ B) = B` (Fomin, Williams and Zelevinsky, *Introduction to cluster algebras, Chapters 1–3*, arXiv:1608.05735v5, Exercise 2.7.7(2)). The proof uses only formula (2.7.1), so it holds for every integer square matrix, skew-symmetrizable or not.
nodes.title: Matrix mutation is an involution

nodes.summary: The mutation of an integer square matrix `B` in direction `k` is the matrix `B'` with `b'ᵢⱼ = -bᵢⱼ` if `i = k` or `j = k`, `b'ᵢⱼ = bᵢⱼ + bᵢₖ bₖⱼ` if `bᵢₖ > 0` and `bₖⱼ > 0`, `b'ᵢⱼ = bᵢⱼ - bᵢₖ bₖⱼ` if `bᵢₖ < 0` and `bₖⱼ < 0`, and `b'ᵢⱼ = bᵢⱼ` otherwise (Fomin, Williams and Zelevinsky, *Introduction to cluster algebras, Chapters 1–3*, arXiv:1608.05735v5, Lemma 2.7.3, equation (2.7.1), and Definition 2.7.6, square…
nodes.title: Matrix mutation

nodes.summary: `mutateSeq w s` applies the seed mutations in the directions listed in `w`, from left to right (Fomin, Williams and Zelevinsky, *Introduction to cluster algebras, Chapters 1–3*, arXiv:1608.05735v5, Definitions 3.1.7–3.1.8: every seed of the seed pattern through `s` is reached this way).
nodes.title: Iterated seed mutation

nodes.summary: For positive integers `b, c`, every term of the rank-two exchange recurrence started at the initial cluster `(X_0, X_1)` of `ℚ(X_0, X_1)` is a Laurent polynomial in `X_0, X_1` with integer coefficients (Fomin, Williams and Zelevinsky, *Introduction to cluster algebras, Chapters 1–3*, arXiv:1608.05735v5, Section 3.2 with Theorem 3.3.1 for the exchange matrices `±[[0, b], [-c, 0]]`; Fomin and Zelevinsky, *Cluster…
nodes.title: Laurent phenomenon in rank two

nodes.summary: For a cluster `x : n → K` in a field `K` and an exchange matrix `B`, the mutation in direction `k` replaces `xₖ` by `xₖ' = (∏_{bᵢₖ > 0} xᵢ^{bᵢₖ} + ∏_{bᵢₖ < 0} xᵢ^{-bᵢₖ}) / xₖ` and keeps the other cluster variables, while `B` becomes `μₖ B` (Fomin, Williams and Zelevinsky, *Introduction to cluster algebras, Chapters 1–3*, arXiv:1608.05735v5, Definition 3.1.3, exchange relation (3.1.2), in the coefficient-free case…
nodes.title: Seed mutation without frozen variables

nodes.summary: `somos4 (m + 4) * somos4 m = somos4 (m + 3) * somos4 (m + 1) + somos4 (m + 2) ^ 2` for every `m` (Fomin, Williams and Zelevinsky, *Introduction to cluster algebras, Chapters 1–3*, arXiv:1608.05735v5, Example 3.4.3).
nodes.title: Somos-4 recurrence

nodes.summary: `somos4 4, …, somos4 9` are `2, 3, 7, 23, 59, 314` (Fomin, Williams and Zelevinsky, *Introduction to cluster algebras, Chapters 1–3*, arXiv:1608.05735v5, Example 3.4.3).
nodes.title: First terms of the Somos-4 sequence

nodes.summary: Every term of the Somos-4 sequence `1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 3, 7, 23, 59, …` is an integer (Fomin, Williams and Zelevinsky, *Introduction to cluster algebras, Chapters 1–3*, arXiv:1608.05735v5, Example 3.4.3, deduced there from the Laurent phenomenon; Fomin and Zelevinsky, *The Laurent phenomenon*, Adv. in Appl. Math. 28 (2002), Example 3.3, Laurentness of the generalized Somos-4 recurrence).
nodes.title: Integrality of the Somos-4 sequence

nodes.summary: Every term of `somos4` is positive, so its defining division is never by zero.
nodes.title: Positivity of the Somos-4 sequence

nodes.summary: `somos4 0 = somos4 1 = somos4 2 = somos4 3 = 1` and `somos4 (m + 4) = (somos4 (m + 3) * somos4 (m + 1) + somos4 (m + 2) ^ 2) / somos4 m`, the recurrence `z_{m+2} z_{m-2} = z_{m+1} z_{m-1} + z_m²` of Fomin, Williams and Zelevinsky, *Introduction to cluster algebras, Chapters 1–3*, arXiv:1608.05735v5, Example 3.4.3, solved for the newest term in `ℚ`.
nodes.title: Somos-4 sequence

can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
